objective: Add organization ID or global to every daily OpenSearch observability index name.
verified_system_context: The timeline collector owns index formatting for all timeline record kinds.
The telemetry OpenSearch exporter owns index formatting for logs, events, and metrics.
Both writers already receive organization ID and preserve it in documents.
Telemetry readers use wildcard patterns that match old and new names.
Bulk write and automatic index creation behavior remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Timeline, logs, events, and metrics include organization ID before the UTC date.
Custom prefixes and document organization fields remain unchanged.
Existing wildcard readers require no code change.
Release owner records archive-cron dry-run evidence before production rollout.
No critical or major review findings remain.

design.organization_segment: Unsigned base-10 organization ID or global for zero
design.date_source: Existing occurrence-time behavior with current UTC fallback for zero timestamps
design.implementation: Modify existing private functions and call sites only

principle_decisions.kiss: Change only two production files and their existing tests.
principle_decisions.yagni: Do not add helpers, configuration, policies, templates, migrations, or lifecycle workers.
principle_decisions.single_source_of_truth: Organization ID comes from the existing scope object used to populate the document.
principle_decisions.compatibility: Preserve custom prefixes, UTC dates, documents, bulk behavior, wildcard reads, and existing indexes.
principle_decisions.failure_safety: Use global when organization context is absent instead of dropping records.
principle_decisions.security: Do not change credentials, permissions, or tenant fields.

risks.risk: Per-organization daily indexes increase index and shard count.
risks.disposition: Accepted for organization-level archival. Release owner monitors cluster health and existing shard limits.

risks.risk: The external cron may not recognize new names.
risks.disposition: Release owner attaches dry-run evidence for old and new names before production deployment.

risks.risk: Organization ID zero combines records in global indexes.
risks.disposition: Accepted to preserve observability delivery when context is unavailable.

risks.risk: Late records can target an old occurrence date.
risks.disposition: Existing behavior is preserved and archive lifecycle remains externally owned.

required_test_categories: UTC occurrence date and zero-time fallback
rollout: Release owner records archive-cron dry-run evidence for old and new names.
Verify index names, document organization IDs, wildcard readers, cluster health, and index count.
rollback: Roll back the application binary. Shared names resume and wildcard readers continue matching both layouts.
